name: Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS) for Mathematics
checked: 2026-10-01: every student expectation for K–5 read from 19 TAC §111.2 to §111.7 (adopted 2012, in force since 2014–15)
note: Summaries are our own one-line wording; the official text stays at the source, and TEA restricts reuse of it. source_url is §111.2 (Kindergarten); rows for Grades 1 to 5 carry their own section (§111.3 to §111.7). Codes are grade.knowledge-statement plus the letter (3.4F); 3.4(F) and 3.4.F are aliases. Knowledge statements are the cluster, not rows. Process standards (x.1A–G) are listed but out of scope: they run through the content items.

standards.summary: Count forward and backward to at least 20, with or without objects.
Read, write and show numbers from 0 to 20 with objects or pictures.
standards.scope_note: Handwriting is not checked; reading numbers and matching them to sets is.

standards.summary: Count a set of up to 20 and know the last number said is how many, however the objects are arranged.

standards.summary: Name the U.S. coins: penny, nickel, dime and quarter.

standards.summary: Name something about an object that can be measured, such as length, capacity or weight.
standards.scope_note: Describing in words is limited to choosing attribute names.

standards.summary: Compare two objects by one attribute and tell which has more or less of it.

standards.scope_note: Gathering is hands-on; sorting given data into groups is on screen.

standards.summary: Make real-object graphs and picture graphs from data.

standards.summary: Answer questions and draw conclusions from real-object and picture graphs.
